answer: A vine teaches me to follow a line before judging where it leads: growth is rarely straight, and the tendrils that reach furthest are the ones that tested each hold along the way. A karst landscape reminds me that what looks solid can be hollowed by slow water, so I check the ground under a claim instead of trusting its surface. A walnut is the smallest test, a hard shell around something worth keeping, and I only count a conclusion as mine once I have cracked it open and found the kernel intact. I keep the method, not just the answer.
